marta.ng: Quick FYI — Q3 usage projection shows a shift: a new partner will send a lot of streaming requests with 8k->32k context windows starting mid-June. We need a short plan for capacity + cost tradeoffs by EOD tomorrow.
sam.lee: Ack. Do we have the split streaming vs non-streaming %s and average token lengths from the ingest? I want to run the throughput sim.
marta.ng: Current sample (last 2 weeks): streaming 42%, non-streaming 58%. Median context for streaming ~9k, tail at ~28k. Overall token mix shift -> +18% tokens / request vs baseline.
ishaan: If those numbers hold, naive scaling of ded­i­cated pools -> ~22% more GPU-hours. But with KV-prefetch + aggressive prefix caching we can avoid ~9-11% of that increase.
lina: Heads up: eu-west1 peering still has egress shaping for some partners. If we push more streaming there we risk queueing at the network edge, which will blow tail latency and trigger retries.
sam.lee: Can we route long-context streaming to dedicated pools in us-central with cross-region policy? That'd add egress $ but reduce retry storms.
ishaan: Routing policy idea: prefer same-region for <12k context, otherwise route to us-central dedicated pool with high-throughput instances. Pseudoconfig:
```
routing:
  - match: request.context_tokens > 12000
    prefer: pool:dedicated-highmem-us-central
    fallback: pool:dedicated-us-central
    max_egress_bytes: 10GB
```
marta.ng: Nice. Also we should try a KV-prefetch job to prepopulate popular prefixes for the partner's top-100 prompts. That reduces token generation by ~600 tokens/request on average in our bench.
sam.lee: I ran a quick sim. Baseline (no caching, current autoscaler): 4 x A100s per shard, 2500 qps sustained -> monthly GPU-hours 14,400. With routing + KV-prefetch we can keep 3.5 x A100s effective -> ~11,900 GPU-hours. Estimated delta: -17% hours vs naive scale but +$1,800/mo egress and control-plane ops.
lina: Are we comfortable with KV prefetch memory footprints? 32k contexts -> KV cache blowups. Need mem-cap check.
ishaan: We should cap KV-prefetch window per model to 12k tokens and use compressed KV pages (4-bit quantized) for prefetch items. Rough footprint calc:
- avg entry size: 46KB (compressed)
- top-100 prefixes -> ~4.6MB per shard
- 200 shards -> 920MB total (fits)
ops-bot: deploy-bot: autoscaler-experiment branch passed canary. CI: 14/14 tests ok. (link: https://ci.redwood/exp/234)
marta.ng: Good. Next steps:
1) Sam: run full-scale sim for 2 traffic profiles (50% and 80% streaming) and attach csv by 14:00 tomorrow.
2) Ishaan: produce a KV-prefetch runbook + mem calc + config for canary (limit 10% of traffic) by EOD.
3) Lina: confirm cross-region egress cost estimates and peering throttling windows with infra-net by EOD.
We want a recommended provisioning plan for Q3 commit by Friday.
sam.lee: Will do. Quick note: if we instead choose to promote quantized model variants for long-context requests we could trade some quality vs compute. I'll include a quality vs cost curve in the sim.
marta.ng: Thanks — please keep replies short. :thumbsup:
